text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Romania's state airline Tarom SA will start renewing its fleet for domestic flights in December. Soviet-made AN-24 aircraft are expected to be replaced in the first stage.
- Romania's central bank signed an accord on a $175 million syndicated loan on international capital markets.
- The over-the-counter market, due to start trading soon, can give fresh investment opportunities to investment funds.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Local bankers agree that a recent forecast putting the leu-dollar rate at 6,000 is farfetched.
ADEVARUL
- Autumn harvest work is delayed due to diesel oil shortages.
- Car maker Volvo is interested in securing a stake of ARO SA, Romanian maker of four-wheel drive cars.
ZIUA
- A shareholders' meeting at troubled Banca Dacia Felix SA will decide whether to approve a bank recovery plan advanced by Swiss holding Winlook Management.
LIBERTATEA
- The central bank acquired $1.5 billion worth of raisings on international capital markets, which will help to increase Romania's hard currency reserves to $1.0 billion this year.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA

- The opposition Social Democratic Party (USD) issues a "final appeal" to the ruling Party of Social Democracy (PDSR) and its presidential candidate, President Ion Iliescu, to end "the dirty and lying campaign" against the USD and its presidential candidate, reformist former Prime Minister Petre Roman.

- The leaders of various parties criticise as an abuse of power the Supreme Court's decision to bar judge Corneliu Turianu from running for the upper house, the Senate, on the list of the opposition Democratic Convention (CDR).

- The opposition CDR will launch its "Contract with the young people", part of its electoral programme for the November 3 elections entitled "Contract with Romania" at the Children's Palace in Bucharest on October 29.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The newspaper presents a report on alleged fraud committed in lists of signatures backing the candidacy for presidency of George Muntean, leader of the Pensioners' Party.

- The newspaper publishes excerpts from "The White Book of the Securitate" written by the Romanian Intelligence Service containing documents from the former Securitate secret police on writers and artists starting 1969. The book will be sold starting Monday.
- One-page report on the "human part" of the USD presidential candidate Petre Roman.
ADEVARUL

- Gyorgy Frunda, presidential candidate of the Hungarian Democratic Union (UDMR), does not rule out forming an alliance with the ruling PDSR if that party changes its attitude over the issue of minorities.
- "Bucharest -- the city with one public toilet for 100,000 citizens" reads the headline on a report on the state of the toilets.
ZIUA
- The newspaper publishes alleged scenarios drawn by the ruling PDSR and President Iliescu to stay in power whatever the outcome of the November 3 elections.
- Judge Turianu says President Iliescu is behind the court's decision to bar him from running for the Senate as revenge against him for challenging Iliescu's new presidential bid in the courtsw.
CRONICA ROMANA
- A 15-year-old girl raped by three gendarmes claims 30 million lei ($9,000) in moral damages.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- "It would not be good for NATO's border to coincide with the Romanian-Hungarian border," said Hungary's Defence Minister Gyorgy Keleti during a visit to Ukraine.
LIBERTATEA
- Half of rape victims are schoolgirls, says the newspaper in a report. Most come from large families in urban areas. ($=3,299 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
